title: Add Strings
statement:
Add two non-negative integers that are written as decimal strings.

Contract
- `first` and `second` are non-null, non-empty, and contain only the digits `0`
  through `9`. Neither has a leading zero unless it is exactly `"0"`.
- Either number may have thousands of digits, far more than a `long` holds.
  Do not convert a whole input to a numeric type or use `BigInteger`.
- Return the sum as a decimal string in the same form: digits only, with no
  leading zeros unless the sum is `"0"`.

Examples
- `addStrings("456", "77")` returns `"533"`.
- `addStrings("1", "999")` returns `"1000"`.
- `addStrings("0", "0")` returns `"0"`.
hints: The inputs can be far longer than any primitive can hold, so parsing them overflows.
Add the way you would on paper: start from the last digit of each string and carry into the next column.

Loop while either string still has digits or a carry remains, append each result digit to a StringBuilder, and reverse it once at the end. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) extra space for the result.
inputSyntax: Input: the two numbers separated by a space, for example: 456 77
